concepts.def: Breakdown of rock in place by freeze-thaw, chemicals or biology.
Wear and removal of material by rivers, waves, ice or wind.
Downslope movement of weathered material under gravity.
Water freezes in cracks, expands and shatters rock.
Plucking and abrasion by ice carve dramatic uplands.
Quarrying, farming and building reshape the surface fast. 🏔

walkthroughs.body_html:
Three families of process matter.

Weathering breaks rocks where they sit.

Erosion removes pieces; mass movement slides them downslope.

Freeze-thaw is common in UK uplands.

Water seeps into cracks, freezes overnight and expands ~9%.

Repeated cycles split rock and build scree slopes.

People are now huge agents of change.

Farming clears woodland; quarrying carves hillsides; cities pave floodplains.

Some changes happen in decades, far faster than nature.
